properties.content: Question: nick chubb injury Answer: Nick Chubb suffered a serious knee injury during the 2023 NFL season and underwent multiple surgeries. He sustained damage to his MCL, medial capsule, meniscus, and ACL. The injury occurred in Week 2 of the 2023 season and was season-ending. While he returned to play for a few games in the 2024 season, he also broke his foot in Week 15. Here's a more detailed breakdown:: - Initial Injury: Chubb sustained a severe knee injury in Week 2 of the 2023 season against the Pittsburgh Steelers. The injury involved hyperextension and inward force to his left knee, potentially causing a dislocation and/or multiple ligament tears. - Surgeries: Chubb had two surgeries to repair the damage. The first surgery, in September 2023, repaired the MCL, medial capsule, and meniscus. The second surgery, in November 2023, repaired the ACL. - Rehabilitation and Return: Chubb spent the remainder of the 2023 season recovering. He returned to practice in October 2024 and played in eight games during the 2024 season before suffering a broken foot in Week 15. - Impact: The knee injury significantly impacted Chubb's performance upon his return. He averaged a career-low 3.3 yards per carry in 2024. - Current Status: After the 2024 season, Chubb became a free agent and signed with the Houston Texans. He believes he is back to his old self and that the injury is behind him, according to NFL.com.
